# ESSA.JK — house coverage rates it BUY (IDEATION re-stamp 2026-11-06)

Signal: house coverage v1 carries a BUY with a Rp941 target against Rp496 (2026-11-05), +89.7% on the probability-weighted scenarios (base 802.5, bear 431.2, bull 1,637.1). Why now: the primary leg is a life DCF at Rp881 (75% weight) with EV/EBITDA 580 and P/E 339 as the minority legs — the target is valuation-anchored, and even the bear case is only −13.1%.

**Regime: NEUTRAL.** The desk has no tilt on ammonia: the commodity bloc is NEUTRAL and explicitly "underwrite name-by-name, do not chase". ESSA produces ammonia and LPG from gas, so it is neither an oil-import beneficiary nor a nickel supply-discipline name; the war premium in energy cuts both ways (product price up, gas input cost up).

Archetype: `commodity_capex_turnaround` · method card: VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL.

**Fast-disqualify checks.** (1) EV at the registry prior (0.42/+75/−35) = **+11.2%** — positive. (2) Target clears: +61.8% at base against a ~20%/yr annualised up-leg. (3) Sources: house model with filed fund record; FY2025 statements reachable.

**Questions for the deep-dive.** Revenue fell from USD731.5m (FY2022) to USD295.0m (FY2025) — how much is ammonia price versus volume, and what is through-cycle EBITDA? What ammonia price does the base case embed, and does it survive the 2027 supply additions the desk flags as an export-tailwind fade? Does the gas input contract re-price with the war premium inside the model's horizon?
